clue.text: Reportedly go stealthily after a wading bird

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for going stealthily is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to stalk is to move stealthily after prey

explanation.surface: A stealthy hunter creeps up behind a heron-like bird in the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech STALK and STORK sound the same, which is what 'Reportedly' relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: The stork is a long-legged bird that feeds by wading in marshes and shallow water.

clue.text: Cheerfully casual friends from south very quietly lying in cut grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, from south means read upwards, so the friends word is backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

indicators.note: lying in means resting inside, so the quiet letters go into the grass word

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: Friends from the south lie very quietly in the mown hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-happy describes someone carefree and happy-go-lucky, casual in a cheerful way.

clue.text: Alternative books originally recommended by governor

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
HE, His Excellency, is the title of a governor

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of recommended is taken

explanation.surface: A governor recommends some other reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Other as an adjective means different or alternative, as in 'the other option'.

clue.text: Position of top man back at last in grand vessel

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of back is taken

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: The top man is back at last on a grand ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingship is the office or status of a king, the top man of a realm.

clue.text: Position of titled person touring Eton by car

indicators.note: touring suggests travelling round and about, so the letters of the following words are moved around

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman motors around Eton in his car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' scrambles ETON BY CAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronetcy is the rank held by a baronet, a hereditary titled commoner below a baron.

clue.text: Brought up cash for speaker?

indicators.note: for speaker means as it would be said aloud by someone

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash

explanation.surface: Was cash raised, the speaker asks?
explanation.definitionFit: Bred, as in well-bred, means raised or reared, the past form of bring up.

clue.text: Striking, like schoolwork submitted a second time?

definitions.text: like schoolwork submitted a second time?
definitions.meaning: taken as ..., able to be marked again

explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means worthy of notice; split, it is whimsically something able to be graded once more.

clue.text: Indigenous trees primarily planted in green

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so the first letter goes into the green word

parts.note: green means inexperienced, naive

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter of trees is taken

explanation.surface: Native trees are mainly planted on the village green.
explanation.definitionFit: Native and indigenous both mean originating naturally in a place.

clue.text: Change coaches delayed leaving India

indicators.note: leaving means the India letter departs from the coaches word

parts.note: trains are made up of coaches
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Coaches that were delayed have to change on leaving India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops I from TRAINS, leaving TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to convert from one form or language to another, to change.

clue.text: Disgusting yobs upsetting kindly Kent youths at first

indicators.note: at first means the first letters of these five words are taken

explanation.surface: Revolting yobs are upsetting the decent young men of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yukky is informal for nasty or revolting, the same as disgusting.

clue.text: Articles by retired chap about Brussels club?

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the other piece
retired means drawn back, so the word for chap is read backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man
Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: Some newspaper pieces by a pensioner about a Brussels club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns MAN into NAM, which goes 'about' EU to give NAEUM. The Athenaeum is a London gentlemen's club; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenaeum is a famous private members' club in Pall Mall, London, so it exemplifies a club.

clue.text: Rough path taking zigzag course across river

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the zigzag word lies across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a tack is a sailing boat's zigzag course into the wind

explanation.surface: A rough path wanders back and forth over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is an unmade path or trail beaten by use, a rough way across country.

clue.text: Badger about to leave African capital by ship

indicators.note: to leave means the word for about goes out of the capital's name

parts.note: Harare is the capital of Zimbabwe
re means about or concerning
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A badger sets off from an African capital by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes RE out of HARARE, leaving HARA.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, the same as harassing them.

clue.text: Touchy about curtailed party — a mockery!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for touchy goes round the shortened party

parts.note: touchy means irritable, testy

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the party word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rave is a large lively party

explanation.surface: Someone irritable complains that a cut-short party was a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy' looks like the definition, but 'a mockery!' is; the touchy word is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque distorted imitation, a mockery of the real thing.

clue.text: Precocious child supported by family in outskirts of Watford

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these go between the outer letters
outskirts of means the outer letters of Watford

parts.note: under means supported by, beneath
kin are family

explanation.surface: A gifted child is backed by relations living on the edge of Watford.
explanation.walkthrough: Watford is a town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A wunderkind, German for wonder child, is a prodigy who achieves success very young.

clue.text: Fussy detail

definitions.meaning: a ... is an individual item or detail, as in 'in every ...'

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fastidious; as a noun it means a single point of information.

clue.text: A door she used at first moving around wayside inn

indicators.note: moving around means the letters shift position, rearranged
at first means the first letter of used

explanation.surface: She at first used a door that swung round into a roadside pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving around' signals the anagram, with the U from 'used at first' included in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or bar on a main road outside a town.

clue.text: Research establishment backing a Welsh lake

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the research establishment word is read backwards

parts.note: a lab, laboratory, is a research establishment

explanation.surface: A research centre supports a lake in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bala Lake, Llyn Tegid, in Gwynedd is the largest natural lake in Wales.

clue.text: Holding line, it rarely disturbed gunners

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the scrambled letters hold the line letter
disturbed means upset, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Holding the line, gunners were rarely troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' signals the anagram and 'Holding' puts L into the mixed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The artillery is the branch of an army that operates big guns, its gunners.

clue.text: Presumptuous fool with posh Chinese porcelain

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U means upper-class, posh
Ming is fine porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: An idiot with fancy Chinese vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming as an adjective means arrogant, taking too much for granted.

clue.text: Chinese currency your aunt regularly used

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of these two words is taken

explanation.surface: Your aunt routinely spent Chinese money.
explanation.definitionFit: The yuan is the basic monetary unit of the People's Republic of China.

clue.text: Youth's rise incorporating state benefit

definitions.note: read as 'Youth is', the definition being Youth

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into its body, so the rise word holds the benefit word

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A young person climbs the ladder by drawing welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person in their teens, which is what an adolescent is.

clue.text: Wear down painter finally settled in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go into Lincoln's name

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of settled

explanation.surface: A painter finally settled in the city of Lincoln, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter' is RA and 'finally settled' D, not the last letter of painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or rub away, wearing a surface down.

clue.text: Classical composer — namely Parry, perhaps?

parts.note: sc., scilicet, is Latin for namely
Sir Hubert Parry was the English composer of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A classical composer is identified: Parry, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: Parry looks like the composer meant, but he only gives his first name, HUBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Schubert was the Austrian composer of the classical-to-romantic era.

clue.text: Slosh around a county bordering on Wales once

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the slosh word wraps round the letter a

parts.note: to slop is to slosh liquid about

explanation.surface: Splashing about in a county by the Welsh border.
explanation.walkthrough: Salop was the official name of Shropshire, an English county on the Welsh border, from 1974 to 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the old abbreviation and former name of Shropshire, which borders Wales.

clue.text: A songbird, or a couple of bovines, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear asks whether the word is being heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: two bovines are a bull and a bull

explanation.surface: Is that birdsong, or just two cattle lowing?
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbul is a songbird of Asia and Africa, celebrated in Persian poetry.

clue.text: Specific type of dramatic poem Ibsen wrote

explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a kind or variety of goods; Ibsen's Brand is a play in verse.

clue.text: Just a tree outside

indicators.note: outside means the tree word goes round the letter a

parts.note: a fir is a tree

explanation.surface: A fair-minded verdict: just a tree standing outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and just both mean impartial, treating everyone equitably.

clue.text: Girl's ultimately regretful feeling

definitions.note: read as 'Girl is', the definition being Girl

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of regretful is taken

parts.note: an aura is a distinctive feeling or atmosphere

explanation.surface: A girl's lingering emotion is one of regret.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a female given name, so a crossword can call it a girl.

clue.text: Spiritless detainee an Italian leader imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned means locked up, so the detainee word holds the other letters

parts.note: an inmate is someone detained in a prison

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: A listless prisoner is an Italian boss behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless or lacking vitality, so spiritless in both senses.

clue.text: E.g. James Stuart, an indulger in make-believe?

definitions.meaning: James Francis Edward Stuart was the Old ..., claimant to the British throne

explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne is a pretender, and so, whimsically, is anyone who plays at make-believe.

clue.text: Devout head of Giggleswick strangely lacking in heart

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of Giggleswick
lacking in heart means the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: oddly means strangely

explanation.surface: The headmaster of Giggleswick school is pious but oddly heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: Giggleswick is a public school in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Godly means pious and religious, the same as devout.
